project.title: Effect of Internal Carbon Source Development and Utilization on Enhanced Nitrogen Removal from Oily Wastewater and the Underlying Microbial Mechanisms
project.description: To address the challenge of consistently meeting the total nitrogen (TN) discharge standard in refinery oily wastewater treatment, this study established both sequencing batch biofilm reactors (SBBRs) and continuous-flow biofilm reactors. The nitrogen removal performance of these systems was systematically investigated under different carrier filling ratios and various process modes, while the succession patterns of the microbial community structure were elucidated using high-throughput sequencing. The SBBR experiments showed that the optimal treatment performance was achieved at a 40% filling ratio, where the TN removal efficiency under the simultaneous nitrification and denitrification (SND) mode was significantly higher than that in reactors with lower filling ratios. The continuous-flow reactor experiments demonstrated that the oxic-anoxic-oxic (OAO) process, through the rational arrangement of anoxic and oxic zones, achieved a much higher TN removal efficiency compared to both the SND process and the anoxic-oxic (AO) process with internal recirculation. Zone-specific water quality monitoring further confirmed that the anoxic zone in the OAO process effectively fulfilled the denitrification function. Microbial community analysis revealed that a high carrier filling ratio favored the directional enrichment of nitrogen-removal-related functional consortia, and the OAO process exhibited a clear pattern of functional differentiation across the zones, i.e., "oxic nitrification - anoxic denitrification - oxic advanced treatment." This study provides an optimized set of process parameters and a microbiological basis for the upgrading and retrofitting of refinery oily wastewater treatment systems to achieve the TN discharge standard.
